messages:
maria: quick sync — we've got weird double-cost spikes when enrichment retries. root cause looks like billing_key getting attached only in enrichment, and retries/emits before enrichment cause downstream counts with no billing key -> later enriched events counted again. anyone familiar with the best pattern for ordering / idempotency here?
vikram: can you paste a minimal repro? my expectation is dedup on trace_id should prevent double counting. are we deduping before or after billing attribution?
maria: repro: ingest -> emit envelope (trace_id=abc123, no billing_key) -> enrichment attempts to fetch tenant, fails, retries, succeeds -> enriched envelope (trace_id=abc123, billing_key=acct42). downstream aggregator sees two events (one without billing_key, one with) and attributes them separately. logs: ```
INGEST: envelope_id=env-7 trace_id=abc123 billing_key=null
ENRICH: envelope_id=env-7 trace_id=abc123 billing_key=acct42
```
tanya: ugh. couple options: 1) best-effort lookup at ingress and stash billing_key (cache misses ok) + add billing_key_source=ingress|enrichment; 2) keep billing resolution in enrichment but emit an idempotency token at ingest (envelope_id) and make aggregator dedupe on envelope_id regardless of billing_key. latter seems simplest.
nate: ingress lookup is risky for p95 latency and also leaks mapping into edge where we might not want to call identity services. I prefer making enrichment idempotent and have it emit a "billing_resolution" event that updates the existing aggregated row instead of creating a new one. it's slightly more work in aggregator but avoids changing ingress.
dkaplan: aggregator updating rows is viable but we need clear ordering semantics. proposal: enrichment writes a small commit record: {"envelope_id":"env-7","billing_key":"acct42","enrichment_anchor_ts":1640000000}. aggregator processes commits in time-windowed batches and uses envelope_id as primary for dedupe + latest commit wins for billing_key. This lets us keep ingest fast and still get correct attribution. tradeoff: delayed visibility until commit window flush.
infra-bot: deploy finished: feature/agg-envelop-dedupe rolled to canary (1 of 3). hash: cb9d4f3 — monitor aggregation-latency metric.
samir: practical caution — using envelope_id as dedupe key is easiest but could increase cardinality in our aggregation index if some clients send unique envelope_id per retry. we should enforce a normalized envelope_id (UUID per logical trace) at ingest or have short TTL dedupe (24h).
tanya: agreed — TTL + best-effort ingress hints seems pragmatic. also add a small flag on envelopes: "billing_tentative": true when billing not yet resolved. aggregator can treat tentative rows as uncommitted and exclude from billing reports until resolved. low engineering overhead.
maria: I like the combined approach: 1) require envelope_id at ingress (generate if missing) 2) mark billing_tentative=true by default 3) enrichment emits commit record with enrichment_anchor_ts and billing_key 4) aggregator dedupes on envelope_id and prefers committed billing_key within 24h window. action items: maria -> add envelope_id validation to edge (ETA 2d), tanya -> proto for commit record (ETA 3d), nate -> aggregator change to support tentative/commit semantics + TTL (ETA 1w). any objections?
vikram: sounds good. only ask: add a telemetry gauge for tentative rows so SRE can monitor unresolved backlog.
maria: noted — will include metric in PR. :thumbsup:
